taxonomic_note: Accepted species. Native to Europe, western/central Asia, and northwestern Africa; introduced in North America including Texas.
look_here_first: Look for the winged spiny stems and harsh prickly foliage. Bull thistle is a coarse biennial with decurrent leaf bases that run down the stem into spiny wings, large purple heads, and strongly spiny phyllaries.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew POWO lists the native range outside North America. Central Texas records are introduced/naturalized, not native.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Naturalized wild occurrence does not count as native county evidence.

best_field_traits: leaf bases decurrent onto stem forming spiny wings
outer and middle phyllaries ending in spreading spines
often disturbed roadsides, pastures, and waste ground
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use the winged spiny stem as the fastest split from most native Central Texas Cirsium. Do not confuse wild naturalization with native status.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. vulgare has conspicuously decurrent leaf bases that create spiny stem wings. Native C. horridulum has spectacularly spiny leaves surrounding the head but does not show the same coarse winged-stem architecture; C. texanum is usually less brutally armed overall.
